views.label: Early date, about 1446 BC
views.who: Reads 1 Kings 6:1 (480 years before Solomon's Temple) as a literal count.

views.label: Late date, 13th century BC
views.who: Links it to the reign of Ramesses II and the Merneptah Stele (about 1208 BC).

views.label: Between 6 and 4 BC
views.who: Most scholars, because Herod the Great died about 4 BC.

views.label: 7 April AD 30
views.who: One of the two dates that fit the Passover calendar and Pilate's term.

views.label: 931 BC
views.who: Edwin Thiele, The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings. Other chronologists differ by a few years.
views.source: Wikipedia, “The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings”

views.label: 586 BC
views.who: Thiele's reign table ends Zedekiah in 586.
views.source: Wikipedia, “The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings”

views.label: 6th century BC
views.who: The traditional view, following the book's setting under Babylon and Persia.

views.label: About 168 to 164 BC
views.who: The majority view in critical scholarship, based on its detail about Antiochus IV.

views.label: Moses, about the 15th or 13th century BC
views.who: The traditional view of the Pentateuch's authorship.

views.label: Final form after the Exile
views.who: The common view in critical scholarship, which sees earlier sources brought together.

views.label: Three parts, 8th century to after the Exile
views.who: The common view in critical scholarship, dividing chapters 1-39, 40-55 and 56-66.

views.label: About AD 70
views.who: The usual date in critical scholarship.

views.label: Before AD 70
views.who: The view of many conservative scholars, who read Mark 13 as prediction.

views.label: Before AD 70
views.who: A minority view. Schaff records that some of the best scholars of his day assigned it to 68 or 69.
views.source: Philip Schaff, History of the Christian Church, vol. 1, on the Apocalypse
